title: Paramartha Guru Tale 78
summary: Six months after the rescue of the Moon from the well, Guru Paramartha stood by the garden well at noon. Looking down into the dark water...
full_text:
Six months after the rescue of the Moon from the well, Guru Paramartha stood by the garden well at noon. Looking down into the dark water, the bright midday sun illuminated the surface, reflecting his own face with crystal clarity.

The Guru stared: 'Look! Another venerable, silver-bearded sage lives at the bottom of our well! He wears a yellow shawl and watches me with profound spiritual curiosity!'

The Guru summoned his disciples: 'Children, a holy ascetic has taken up residence in our aquatic depths! We must converse with him on the nature of reality!'

Matti leaned over the rim and shouted down the stone shaft: 'REVERED SAGE OF THE DEPTHS! GREETINGS FROM GURU PARAMARTHA!'

The deep, echo-chamber of the circular masonry wall immediately echoed back with hollow resonance: 'GREETINGS FROM GURU PARAMARTHA!'

Matti gasped in awe: 'He answers! He speaks our master's name with profound reverence!'

Madayan shouted down: 'WHAT IS YOUR PHILOSOPHICAL DOCTRINE?'

The well echoed: 'PHILOSOPHICAL DOCTRINE!'

Madayan turned to the Guru with shining eyes: 'He belongs to the Echo School of Veda! He repeats the divine Word!'

The Guru decided to test his hospitality: 'Are you thirsty, holy brother? Shall we lower a pitcher of buttermilk?'

The well echoed: 'BUTTERMILK!'

Peedan lowered a large clay pitcher filled with sweet buttermilk down the well on a rope.

When the pitcher reached the surface, Peedan jerked the cord to offer it. The heavy clay pot struck the rocky wall, shattered to pieces, and twenty pints of white buttermilk poured into the water, clouding the well like milk!

The reflection of the Guru dissolved in the white liquid.

Matti peered down and cheered: 'He drank it! He drank the entire pitcher of buttermilk in a single gulp, and turned the entire lake white with spiritual bliss!'

Guru Paramartha nodded in deep satisfaction: 'A thirsty scholar indeed! May his meditation in our well be blessed!'

And for three days, the ashram drank white buttermilk-water, rejoicing in the presence of their aquatic colleague.
moral: A reflection remains an illusion, whether it wears silver or yellow silk.
